turns.userText:
# Audit a synthetic QUIC receiver

Implement `/app/submission/entry.py`, a defensive, offline QUIC v1 trace auditor. A starter and public examples are in `/app`. Your program reads one UTF-8 JSON docu

records.name: bash
records.summary: echo TMPDIR=$TMPDIR; ls -ld /tmp; python3 -I /app/submission/entry.py < /app/examples/basic.json | head -c 500; echo; echo rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

records.name: bash
records.summary: cd /workspace/tmp && time python3 -I /app/submission/entry.py < big.json > big.out.json; echo rc=$?; ls -l big.out.json; python3 - << 'PY'

records.name: bash
records.summary: find / -maxdepth 4 \( -name '*.json' -o -name '*.py' \) 2>/dev/null | grep -v '/usr/lib/python' | grep -v '/usr/local/lib/python' | grep -v site-packages | head

records.name: bash
records.summary: cd /workspace/tmp && time python3 -I /app/submission/entry.py < big2.json > big2.out3.json && cmp big2.out.json big2.out3.json && echo identical || echo differe

records.name: bash
records.summary: grep -n 'delivered\|contiguous' /app/submission/entry.py | head -50; wc -c /app/submission/entry.py; python3 -m py_compile /app/submission/entry.py && echo comp
